students.name: Mr. Venkatesh Jugal
students.biography: A research scholar in Applied Botany, specializing in plant ecology, biodiversity, and molecular phylogeny, with doctoral research focused on the genus *Nothopegia* Blume, an endemic and ecologically significant tree genus of the Western Ghats. My research explores the diversity, distribution, and ecological relationships of Nothopegia species, emphasizing the influence of climatic and edaphic factors on their distribution across the Central Western Ghats of Karnataka. My work integrates field-based ecological investigations, vegetation analysis, soil and climatic assessments, and molecular techniques to understand species relationships and evolutionary patterns. Alongside my research, I am interested in plant taxonomy, forest ecology, phytochemistry, medicinal plants, and biodiversity conservation, with a broader commitment to understanding plant–environment interactions and contributing to the conservation of the unique flora of the Western Ghats.

students.name: Ms. Gagana S. Sathish Kumar
students.biography:
I am a researcher specializing in molecular entomology, protein biochemistry, and translational omics. My research focuses on parasitoid wasps, particularly Trichogramma species, and the molecular mechanisms involved in host–parasitoid interactions.

My work involves the identification and characterization of venom-associated and host-immunosuppressive molecules using transcriptomics, proteomics. I also have experience in recombinant protein expression, Ni–NTA affinity purification, buffer exchange, and functional evaluation of bioactive proteins, including serpins.

The broader objective of my research is to identify novel molecules with potential applications in sustainable biological pest management and biomedical research. I am particularly interested in the immunomodulatory, wound-healing, and therapeutic potential of parasitoid-derived proteins, as well as polydnaviruses, venom evolution, and the integration of insect molecular biology with translational science.

students.name: Ms. Sneha M. A. Anthony
students.biography:
My research focuses on the synthesis of heterocyclic compounds through green catalytic approaches and conventional organic synthetic methodologies, with particular emphasis on exploring their potential biological applications. I am also actively involved in the synthesis and development of agrochemically important molecules, particularly isoxazolones, and investigating their potential applications as herbicidal, pesticidal, and fungicidal agents.

In addition to my research activities, I serve as a full-time Lecturer in the Postgraduate Department of Chemistry, where I teach and mentor Master's students. I am passionate about creating a supportive and student-friendly academic environment, providing guidance not only in academic development but also in students' overall well-being. I strongly believe in approachable teaching, effective communication, and student counselling to help learners manage academic challenges and stress while developing confidence and independent thinking.

Beyond my regular teaching responsibilities, I actively conduct coaching classes for competitive examinations, particularly KSET and CSIR-UGC NET, to support students aspiring to pursue careers in higher education and research.

I am enthusiastic about academic and research collaborations within my areas of expertise and welcome opportunities for interdisciplinary research and teaching initiatives. I am particularly interested in collaborative projects that integrate organic synthesis, green chemistry, medicinal chemistry, biological sciences, and agricultural sciences to address scientific challenges and contribute to sustainable development.
